history.name: Euler's officers
history.statement: no Latin square of order $n\equiv2\bmod4$ decomposes into transversals

milestones.text: false for every other such $n>2$ (Bose, Shrikhande, Parker)

history.name: Hall–Paige
history.statement: a group table has a transversal iff the Sylow $2$-subgroups are trivial or non-cyclic

history.name: Ryser
history.statement: every Latin square of odd order has a transversal

history.name: Ryser–Brualdi–Stein
history.statement: every Latin square has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells
history.where: Conj. 2.19, Thm 2.21

history.name: Stein
history.statement: every equi-$n$-square has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells

milestones.text: full transversal if each symbol appears $\leq(n-1)/16$ times (Erdős–Spencer)
$n-n^{1-\Omega(1)}$ cells, and $n-\Omega(\sqrt n)$ is best possible (Chakraborti et al.)

history.name: Kotzig
history.statement: $K_{2n}$ has a perfect $1$-factorisation

milestones.text: true when $2n-1$ or $n$ is prime

history.name: Aharoni–Berger (bipartite)
history.statement: $n$ matchings of size $n+1$ in a bipartite multigraph have a full rainbow matching

milestones.text: size $2n$ by a greedy argument

history.name: Aharoni–Berger ($r$-partite)
history.statement: $2^{r-1}(t-1)+1$ matchings of size $t$ in an $r$-partite $r$-graph have a rainbow matching of size $t$

milestones.text: the right number has order $t^r$ (Pohoata–Sauermann–Zakharov)

history.name: Ringel
history.statement: $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into copies of any tree with $n$ edges
history.where: Conj. 3.13, Thm 3.14

history.name: Graceful tree
history.statement: every tree is graceful

milestones.text: almost all trees almost graceful (Adamaszek et al.)
bijective labelling with few repeated differences (Letzter–Pokrovskiy–Williams)

history.name: Brualdi–Hollingsworth
history.statement: every optimal colouring of $K_{2n}$ decomposes into rainbow spanning trees
history.where: Conj. 3.3, Thm 3.7

history.name: Rota's basis conjecture
history.statement: $n$ bases of a rank-$n$ space split into $n$ rainbow bases

milestones.text: the Alon–Tarsi conjecture for $n$ implies it (Huang–Rota), so it holds in characteristic $0$ for $n=p\pm1$

history.where: Conj. 3.16, Thm 3.18

history.name: Hahn / Andersen
history.statement: proper colourings of $K_n$ have a rainbow Hamilton path (Hahn), or a path on $n-1$ vertices (Andersen)
history.where: Conj. 4.1, Thm 4.2

history.name: Hahn–Thomassen
history.statement: colour classes of size $\alpha n$ force a rainbow Hamilton cycle in $K_n$

milestones.text: classes just below $n/2$ can fail (Pokrovskiy–Sudakov)

history.name: Frieze–Krivelevich
history.statement: colour classes of size $\alpha n$ force every bounded-degree spanning tree

milestones.text: every graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ with classes $n/(51\Delta^2)$ (Böttcher–Kohayakawa–Procacci)

history.name: Graham
history.statement: every $S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p\setminus\{0\}$ has an ordering with distinct partial sums

milestones.text: small sets by the polynomial method and rectification

history.where: Conj. 4.6, Thm 4.7

history.name: Caccetta–Häggkvist / Aharoni
history.statement: outdegree $r$ (resp. colour classes of size $r$) forces a (rainbow) cycle of length $\leq\lceil n/r\rceil$
history.where: Conj. 4.12, Conj. 4.13

history.name: Keevash–Mubayi–Sudakov–Verstraëte
history.statement: $Cn\log n$ edges in a proper colouring force a rainbow cycle

history.name: Brouwer
history.statement: every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has a matching with $(n-4)/3$ edges

milestones.text: $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges for large $n$ (Montgomery)

history.name: Rainbow arborescence
history.statement: $n-1$ spanning arborescences have a rainbow spanning arborescence
